reservoir_ep22_001.speaker: narrator
reservoir_ep22_001.text: On One Thousand Three Hundred Fifty-four, Yue entered the low receiving room while her cultivation record still named the earned small circuit. Mei had the reviewed qualifying sequence on the table. Jing held the accepted sample sources, Deng the finite teaching observations requested from him. None had become interchangeable because the candidate liked them all. The independent decision would describe six actual dates and the local conditions they supported. Yue sat at the ordinary low chair, keeping her shoulder inside the old comfortable range and letting the unissued title remain unissued until Mei spoke.

reservoir_ep22_002.speaker: narrator
reservoir_ep22_002.text: Mei read the preregistered local criteria before the decision: at least seventy-two actually usable after sampling, registered work and sleep; at least ninety-two percent compatible; balanced response through changed temperature, movement and interrupted sleep; full grounding at ordinary stops; and three actual next-day checks after independently recovered trials. These were the conditions stated before the early failures. The record showed them met on the qualifying dates, with real tissue reviews and deductions. No quiet peak or incomplete task had been used as a substitute for an uncompleted changed condition.

reservoir_ep22_003.speaker: narrator
reservoir_ep22_003.text: The temperature trial on Three Hundred Twenty had left seventy-two and three eighths after its quarter-unit sampling total and half-unit familiar task, at ninety-two and one quarter percent compatibility. Its next morning's fresh quarter-unit sample had left seventy-two and one eighth, with the accepted current balance and tissue condition. Mei named both actual dates and sources. Yue heard the arithmetic without trying to hold the larger trial number as today's inventory. This first pair had happened, and its particular evidence belonged to the certificate rather than the best story she could tell about warmth.

reservoir_ep22_004.speaker: narrator
reservoir_ep22_004.text: The movement trial on Thirty-four had left seventy-two and a half, at ninety-two and a half percent compatible. Its next morning's actual fresh sample had left seventy-two and a quarter. The changed-sleep trial on Forty-eight had left seventy-two and a quarter, at ninety-two and one quarter percent, and its next morning's sample had left seventy-two. Each had a recovered starting review, bounded familiar task, full stop and actual tissue check. Mei kept the different dates and quantities visible. The completed series could support the decision without averaging away its smaller margins.

reservoir_exam_certified.speaker: narrator
reservoir_exam_certified.text: Mei issued the independent local certificate on One Thousand Three Hundred Fifty-four: Qi Gathering, stage eight, Balanced reservoir. The actual three changed trials and their real next mornings had all met the preregistered conditions, with the reviewed sources accepted. Yue's earned stage advanced only now. The certificate named retention and control in the tested lower-reservoir practice. It granted no stronger breath throughput, larger load, wider range, healing, shielding or flight. The old shoulder limits remained. She accepted a real advancement supported by specific completed evidence, rather than a title whose useful scope had been left to rumor.

reservoir_ep22_006.speaker: narrator
reservoir_ep22_006.text: Jing handed her the permitted certificate copy after Mei's actual signature and ordinary receiving mark were complete. The fuller independent record stayed with its named custodian. Yue could carry the copy and her own allowed practice notes; the sample sleeves, instruments and prepared stock remained shared property. The certificate's dated trial values were seventy-two and three eighths, seventy-two and a half and seventy-two and a quarter after their actual costs. They were prior recorded results, not a guarantee that every future arrival would hold those quantities after travel or work.

reservoir_ep22_007.speaker: narrator
reservoir_ep22_007.text: Deng congratulated her on a real balanced reservoir and retained the same familiar application ceiling. No ordinary breath could exceed an eighth unit without a separate measured qualified clearance; the familiar four-breath task still used at most half a unit for its already rated quarter-unit useful output. The local stage did not clear a different task or shoulder range. Yue thanked him for instruction in stopping, which sounded smaller than the certificate and had made it possible. His paid teaching work had remained distinct from Mei's independent acceptance all the way through.

reservoir_ep22_008.speaker: narrator
reservoir_ep22_008.text: Yue wanted to stand and announce the result to everybody before the room was cleared. Jing asked her to wait until the actual sleeve was safely away, and she obeyed. The ordinary request made her laugh quietly at herself. Advancement had not removed impatience in the instant it was issued. She could notice and stop an impulse beside the new title rather than pretend the title made every impulse wise. When the instruments were secure, she stood from the low chair and went to lunch with a certificate that could remain true in an ordinary body.

reservoir_ep22_009.speaker: narrator
reservoir_ep22_009.text: At the kitchen table Tian offered a fish holding a miniature low shelf. Yue asked what the shelf meant. He said it was the largest useful thing the fish had actually been cleared to carry. Jing accused him of finally respecting physical scope in art. They laughed and placed the private drawing beside the beans. Fu congratulated Yue on the completed evidence rather than a hidden genius suddenly recognized. The meal's warmth came from friends who had lived the months beside her, including the days when the honest room had said she was not ready.

reservoir_ep22_010.speaker: narrator
reservoir_ep22_010.text: Fu's brother sang the whole song after eating and asked whether Yue wanted a different final rhyme for the new stage. She preferred the current one because its ordinary repair had its own history. He accepted that preference and kept the line. A certificate could change her known cultivation without rewriting relationships into a better version of the past. She had apologized, listened and missed particular meals under particular choices. Those facts stayed. The actual garden audience was pleased to have her there now, not required to claim every earlier absence had been harmless.

reservoir_ep22_011.speaker: narrator
reservoir_ep22_011.text: The pump candidate congratulated her and admitted he still envied the issued record. Yue thanked him for both honest sentences. His next recovered decision had its own actual source and examiner. She offered ordinary company and no method beyond her qualified scope. The certificate did not make her a teacher of every small circuit or a healer of discouragement. He accepted a bean cake and told her the village cat had stolen another fish. They laughed, and the life he meant to return to stayed more concrete than a ranking between their present stages.

reservoir_ep22_012.speaker: narrator
reservoir_ep22_012.text: On the public board Qiu posted the exact issued scope and qualifying dates. The ordinary clerk kept the current certificate separate from any future task clearance. A visitor asked whether stage eight meant Yue could reinforce a carriage axle. Qiu referred him to the actual qualified repair process. The independent reservoir test had examined no such application. Yue heard the question without growing angry at the visitor's hope. She would have to keep explaining actual scope after advancement, especially when a new title made an untested ability sound plausible to somebody who needed it.

reservoir_ep22_013.speaker: narrator
reservoir_ep22_013.text: At the public bank that afternoon, Yue watched ordinary water pass the reed and felt neither a universal revelation nor a new current quantity. The old metaphors remained useful pictures, with limits. Her actual body had earned a more dependable reservoir under three specific changes. It had not become the basin's owner or the answer to every request made beside it. She walked the sound path at ordinary speed, kept the shoulder comfortable and returned before fatigue. The newly issued stage could accompany that plain decision without needing to display itself.

reservoir_ep22_014.speaker: narrator
reservoir_ep22_014.text: Jing asked whether Yue wanted to see the fuller record once more before it went to its archive shelf. She chose a particular page: the original stopped sleep task beside the later actual full release. Both remained. The early headache and paid recovery had not vanished beneath the certificate. They showed why the course reserved care before demanding difficult work. Yue thanked Jing for keeping the cost and awkward beginning visible. A finished practice could be more trustworthy when its history included real failure, rather than require everyone to remember her as ready from the first morning.

reservoir_ep22_015.speaker: narrator
reservoir_ep22_015.text: On One Thousand Three Hundred Fifty-five, Yue completed the family result letter and paid one actual copper for its private dispatch from received personal money. She reported the issued local stage-eight certificate, its three dated trials and actual next-day checks. She wrote the unchanged breath ceiling and shoulder range plainly. No healing method had been tested, and the mother's lost years remained irreversible. Then she described the fish carrying a shelf, the song's retained rhyme and the kitchen celebration. The daughter sent actual news from a life, asking for no quick reply to validate it.

reservoir_ep22_016.speaker: narrator
reservoir_ep22_016.text: The letter's final ordinary question concerned the plum tree's fruit rent. Yue knew its answer might arrive after she departed the basin and be forwarded through the proper private receiving route. The mother retained her own work, helper schedule and household choices. The daughter did not ask her to travel to admire the certificate or rearrange paid care because the course had ended favorably. Their actual selected visit had already changed conversations and work. This new correspondence could continue affection without assigning another household an unpaid role as witness to every advancement.

reservoir_ep22_017.speaker: narrator
reservoir_ep22_017.text: Zhou invited Yue to the ordinary receiving house that afternoon. Her funded course duties had been completed and paid, with the family-calendar allocation settled with its actual worker. He wanted to congratulate a colleague, not reopen an extra wage line. Tian had moved the fish safely below the current dates and the new clerk could check supported sources without Yue watching. The house would continue. Yue felt proud of that ordinary competence and a little sad to no longer be needed there every posted day. The certificate did not require others to become less useful around her.

reservoir_ep22_018.speaker: narrator
reservoir_ep22_018.text: At the farewell tea Zhou asked which work she hoped to accept next. Yue said she would hear the actual finite basin offers before choosing. A public observer role, maintenance service or departure each could have meaningful ordinary costs. Her certificate would not supply a permanent salary or apparatus. Zhou approved the concrete answer and offered no imagined post to ease the uncertainty. The course meals would continue through Fifty-nine; her own money already reserved the following ten days. She could make the later choice without depend on unreceived wages to pay for a bed tonight.

reservoir_ep22_019.speaker: narrator
reservoir_ep22_019.text: On Fifty-six, the actual course receiver began closing the delivered allocation. The received eight hundred eighty had a real source: four hundred eighty from the teaching trust, two hundred forty from the regional work-study guild and one hundred sixty from the separate basin training fund. It had bought the finite course, independent examination, known instruction, ordinary wages and actual care. The old two-hundred-copper grain commission and thirty-copper water project stayed closed under their own sources. A favorable certificate did not let this purse absorb their costs or turn their unused rights into private property.

reservoir_ep22_020.speaker: narrator
reservoir_ep22_020.text: The food and bed ceiling had been five hundred sixty for the two hundred eighty actual calendar days from One Thousand Eighty through Three Hundred Fifty-nine. The held bed had cost one per day for a real reserved place. Actual meals were charged only while Yue attended. Her selected family absence had returned its unused daily meal reserve to the teaching source at the actual reconciliation. Those twenty-two or twenty-three coppers had not become road money. The final present meals still lay through Fifty-nine, so their actual delivery would be checked before the course account closed.

reservoir_ep22_021.speaker: narrator
reservoir_ep22_021.text: Mei's fixed seventy-two-copper independent fee had paid the agreed examination work regardless of pass or failure. Eighteen had paid Jing's finite instrument custody, and eighteen had paid Deng's licensed instruction within the already-earned small-circuit methods. The favorable result added no pass-conditioned bill or bonus. The actual professional and custody work had been delivered within their agreed packages. Yue had seen how independence mattered during the earlier failures. The final course receiver kept these sources distinct from ordinary candidate wages, even though the same familiar people had also shared jokes and meals.

reservoir_ep22_022.speaker: narrator
reservoir_ep22_022.text: Fifty-two planned material coppers had actually supplied the original twelve consumed in failed assessments and forty in accepted ordinary blanks, sampling preparation and practice stock across the course. The separate twelve recovery-replacement coppers had paid the actually issued stock used for the recovered qualifying series. They did not erase the original consumption or appear twice under the planned line. Jing accepted the final custody inventory and retained shared reusable instruments. Yue acquired none. A finished certificate could be carried on paper while the material tools that made it honest stayed with their actual owners.

reservoir_ep22_023.speaker: narrator
reservoir_ep22_023.text: The ninety-six-copper ordinary wage line had paid thirty-two actual eight-hour equivalents to their real workers. Every current duty source had been checked before payment. The earlier family-calendar release or retention had already been settled when its two actual days occurred; no unearned wage remained waiting for Yue to claim at closure. Twenty-five shared post-visit duties had paid seventy-five, beside the actual earlier work. The receiver closed the full funded line without rename every payment as the candidate's personal salary. Choosing a visit had changed which person actually earned part of it.

reservoir_ep22_024.speaker: narrator
reservoir_ep22_024.text: The separate fifty-two-copper recovery reserve had delivered sixteen for four actual post-failure clinical reviews, twenty-four for eight actual protected days and twelve for the received replacement material. The formal next-day qualification checks had their own twelve-copper line, actually paid on Three Hundred Twenty-one, Thirty-five and Forty-nine. All care had real dates and sources. The final result did not make the early stopped work painless or refund its body costs. It showed a course capable of funding the recovery that allowed later evidence to exist without depending on unpromised charity.

reservoir_ep22_025.speaker: narrator
reservoir_ep22_025.text: Yue reviewed the personal payments only after the shared account was clear. Completed grain and course wages, the retained protected-recovery allowance and original travel contingency belonged to her actual private plan. Her family trip and ordinary letters had spent real money. The future post-course food and bed and road had reserved received sources. No shared meal credit, sample sleeve, private water diary or unperformed future term entered that purse. She could leave with modest earned means and permitted own notes rather than an institution's property renamed a reward for advancement.

reservoir_ep22_026.speaker: narrator
reservoir_ep22_026.text: On Fifty-seven the basin owners received eighteen actual coppers for one finite water-service offer, twelve from a civic water-service grant and six from cooperative service charges. Their accepted purposes permitted either bounded public observation or funded maintenance receiving work. The source could support only the selected contract. Rotation would use nine and return nine unspent to the source; maintenance would use all eighteen; departure would accept no new role and return all eighteen. No decision had been made yet. Qiu kept the received purse with its actual owner while the terms were prepared for Yue to read.

reservoir_ep22_027.speaker: narrator
reservoir_ep22_027.text: The proposed public rotation role had limited ratified comparative records, no owned apparatus and two actual remote receiving intervals after departure. Its nine divided into three wages, four dispatch and two approved copies. The proposed maintenance service had ordinary local work and later operating correspondence, with eighteen divided into twelve wages, four dispatch and two forms. Departure retained completed wages and permitted own observations without new basin endorsement. These were real different agreements, not titles attached to the same unchanged work. Their actual dates and scope would be read before a choice.

reservoir_ep22_028.speaker: narrator
reservoir_ep22_028.text: Fu asked whether Yue wanted to know which offer she personally preferred. Yue welcomed the opinion without asking it to decide. Fu liked public observation because she wanted household questions heard accurately, and would also respect a departure with no new duty. Jing valued a funded physical operating record and warned against pretending its forms included private comparative testimony. Yue listened to their particular interests. The issued stage eight did not make the next choice obvious. It opened a possibility of more dependable work whose real human and resource consequences still needed to be chosen.

reservoir_ep22_029.speaker: narrator
reservoir_ep22_029.text: On Fifty-eight Deng supervised a modest familiar release under the new earned stage, retaining the old physical ceiling. Yue felt pleased enough to want a longer set and stopped at the agreed boundary. The certificate described balance, not immunity to a flattering mood. Deng thanked her for months of honest reporting, including the ugly pauses. She thanked him for finite teaching that had never asked her to hide a headache to preserve a planned ending. They finished the actual lesson and left new tasks for separate qualified decisions rather than append them as a celebration.

reservoir_ep22_030.speaker: narrator
reservoir_ep22_030.text: That evening the garden meal contained ordinary beans from the newest row and an argument about the bird's latest basket. Yue ate beside Fu, Jing and Tian, holding the certificate in her private folder instead of displaying it over the table. Friends could know the actual advancement and still argue about art. The mother letter had been dispatched through its ordinary route, with no instant reply invented to complete the moment. Yue's remaining course food would be delivered tomorrow, then her own ten-day living reserve would begin. The next finite agreement remained an actual choice she had not yet made.

reservoir_ep22_031.speaker: narrator
reservoir_ep22_031.text: On One Thousand Three Hundred Fifty-nine, the final course breakfast was actually delivered. The kitchen porter asked Yue whether she preferred the last onion slice or another spoon of beans. She chose the onion and thought of the earliest cold soup trade. Two hundred eighty calendar days had made the table familiar, with actual absences in the middle. Familiarity would not extend its funded meals beyond today. She ate slowly, thanking the porter for the particular ordinary care of asking, rather than offer an impossible promise to remember every bowl perfectly.

reservoir_ep22_032.speaker: narrator
reservoir_ep22_032.text: The ordinary receiver closed actual meal attendance at the end of the day. The bed had been reserved for the full finite term, and present meals delivered on their actual days. Twenty-two or twenty-three unused meal coppers from the selected family absence had returned to the teaching source. Every other ratified line had actually delivered its work, materials or care. Net course spending was eight hundred fifty-eight under the earlier absence or eight hundred fifty-seven under the later. The received eight hundred eighty had no missing expense renamed private travel money at its successful end.

reservoir_ep22_033.speaker: narrator
reservoir_ep22_033.text: Yue signed only the candidate's actual receipt and private-property return conditions, not the independent result she was unqualified to issue herself. Jing accepted that no shared sample tool, sleeve or apparatus had entered the light bag. The ordinary room key remained under its receiving arrangement. Deng's paid teaching package had been delivered, Mei's fixed independent work completed, and the real formal clinical checks paid. The course could close with genuine advancement and exact property still separated. Yue did not need to acquire the instruments to make the certificate feel more substantial.

reservoir_ep22_034.speaker: narrator
reservoir_ep22_034.text: Zhou came to the closing meal with the basket drawing now creased from actual handling. He asked whether she wanted a cleaner version before leaving. Yue preferred the one her friends had held and laughed over. Its imperfection belonged to the private gift, whose giver had offered it freely. The actual wage board remained with its ordinary workers. Her certificate copy and permitted own notes could travel. There was no storage measure she had earned the right to take merely because its familiar swollen rim had helped her understand an honest current comparison.

reservoir_ep22_035.speaker: narrator
reservoir_ep22_035.text: The new clerk thanked Yue for teaching him to ask which actual date a mark described. She told him he had done real work with that habit and would keep learning after she left. He still sometimes guessed a familiar owner before the source arrived. He admitted it and showed how he caught the last guess before copying. Their conversation let useful learning remain incomplete and durable. The received stage eight did not make Yue a flawless mentor; the clerk's improving work did not make every future board free of mistakes. They could continue ordinary exactness without either myth.

reservoir_ep22_036.speaker: narrator
reservoir_ep22_036.text: Tian objected that the farewell was becoming too sensible and presented a final fish with an impossible number of fins. Yue asked whether its maker wanted critique. He wanted admiration without a census. She supplied it. Jing laughed and allowed the fish beside the bowl as long as its tail did not enter the food. An ordinary private gift could have an extravagance the independent record could not. Yue enjoyed that difference. She would carry both a precise certificate and ridiculous drawings, each useful within the purpose its actual giver had chosen.

reservoir_ep22_037.speaker: narrator
reservoir_ep22_037.text: Fu's brother sang the version with the retained invented rhyme, then asked whether Yue would hear another if she stayed under new terms. She said she would attend when her actual duty and recovery calendar allowed, not accept a promise to be present every time. He complained mildly and agreed. The new stage might change her work, but it did not create endless ordinary hours. Fu appreciated the specific answer because she had heard too many people promise affection by offering time they would later have to take from somebody else's accepted appointment.

reservoir_ep22_038.speaker: narrator
reservoir_ep22_038.text: After the meal Fu and Yue walked the sound garden path. Fu wanted to know whether departure had begun to feel attractive because the certificate was complete. It had. Yue also wanted to remain useful in a bounded basin role and feared missing the ordinary faces she had come to know. Fu heard the conflicting wishes without trying to make one prove the other insincere. A real offer tomorrow would name actual work, rights and absence. The choice could become clear enough to make while still leaving a particular life she would miss.

reservoir_ep22_039.speaker: narrator
reservoir_ep22_039.text: At the public bench Yue read the certificate's scope once more. The lower reservoir had retained usable balance through the local three changed conditions and actual next mornings. The present inventory would still be measured at its own dates, with actual costs. The old breath ceiling and shoulder range remained. She had earned no middle or upper center, no Foundation change and no healing of lost years. The exactness made the title less spectacular than some people expected. It made it more useful to a daughter planning work she could actually complete.

reservoir_ep22_040.speaker: narrator
reservoir_ep22_040.text: A passing traveler asked whether the issued stage had made the family visit worthwhile. Yue said the visit had completed ordinary conversations and changed actual duty attendance on its own dates. It had not been a cultivation technique waiting for a favorable retrospective judgment. Her mother had welcomed her before the later certificate. The cousin's meal had either been attended or missed under the real calendar already lived. The traveler accepted the answer after a pause. Yue liked being able to give advancement its actual place without make every prior kindness seem conditional on it.

reservoir_ep22_041.speaker: narrator
reservoir_ep22_041.text: Qiu met her at the ordinary receiving shelf with the fully prepared later offers. The choice appointment would be Three Hundred Sixty, after the course had actually closed. The common eighteen-copper water-service source had its ratified purposes, and unused money would return to its owner under the selected alternative. This offer did not include free room or meals after the course. Yue's ten-day personal living reserve would cover Sixty through Sixty-nine, two per day for actual food and bed. The possible new wages would be added only after their actual work, never used to justify today's solvency.

reservoir_ep22_042.speaker: narrator
reservoir_ep22_042.text: The observer terms named two remote receiving intervals after ordinary departure: four hours on Three Hundred Eighty-eight and four on Four Hundred Twenty-eight. Those eight actual hours formed one accepted ordinary equivalent, paid three only after both were complete. The ratified role permitted limited comparative copies within the owners' public scope, not private diaries or apparatus. Its four dispatch and two copy coppers stayed with the cooperative source until their actual use. Nine of the common eighteen would be allocated; the other nine would return unspent. The finite role would close by Four Hundred Forty-five.

reservoir_ep22_043.speaker: narrator
reservoir_ep22_043.text: The maintenance terms named three local eight-hour days on Three Hundred Sixty-one, Sixty-two and Sixty-four, then four local preparation hours on Sixty-six. Two remote hours on Three Hundred Ninety-two and two on Four Hundred Thirty would complete the final eight-hour equivalent. Thirty-two hours in all would pay twelve actual wages. Nine were due after the three physical days; the last three remained withheld until the actual remote four hours finished after preparation. Four dispatch and two form coppers completed the eighteen. Operating records only, no private comparative testimony, tools or apparatus ownership followed the contract.

reservoir_ep22_044.speaker: narrator
reservoir_ep22_044.text: Departure terms accepted no new role. All eighteen would return to the ordinary source rather than become a farewell gift. Yue would retain her completed personal wages, private certificate copy and permitted own observations, with no basin endorsement or service obligation following her. The ordinary road to Lantern would still be privately booked, and household correspondence remain her own choice. Declining another contract would close a meaningful opportunity for work and scoped records. It would not erase the actual earned stage or confiscate income already paid for performed course duties.

reservoir_ep22_045.speaker: narrator
reservoir_ep22_045.text: Qiu explained why the owners offered one role. The public observer would receive comparative questions independently of the maintenance service's operating work. Combining both under Yue would confuse those separate responsibilities and exceed the finite accepted offer, even if some calendar hours looked physically compatible. The owners had ratified particular sources and budgets, not an invitation to collect every useful title. Yue could select one role or leave. The unchosen work would remain with its actual future process, rather than hide inside a contract whose ordinary heading sounded broad enough to include it.

reservoir_ep22_046.speaker: narrator
reservoir_ep22_046.text: The three offers would end their basin receiving rights and duties by Four Hundred Forty-five. No local tool would travel to Lantern, no private household original would be transferred and no paid bay worker would become free labor for another institution. The owners had identified the regional ordinary receiving desks that could accept the bounded correspondence after departure. Yue could read the current scope before giving an actual answer. The finite deadline would allow the next book of her life to begin with concrete obligations, rather than an institutional title that never stopped requiring unnamed work.

reservoir_ep22_047.speaker: narrator
reservoir_ep22_047.text: Fu listened to the terms and asked whether the remote duties would interfere with ordinary livelihood in Lantern. Qiu showed their actual intervals rather than answer from optimism. The observer's second interval came after the regional documentary work window then under consideration; maintenance's last two hours also came afterward. Yue would still need to report and decline any future incompatible task, because a current compatible outline did not own another place's calendar. The dates gave her a real basis to plan. They did not guarantee every later employer would make space for the basin out of gratitude.

reservoir_ep22_048.speaker: narrator
reservoir_ep22_048.text: Jing asked what each role would permit Yue to carry. The observer could carry only the ratified limited comparative copies and allowed personal notes, with ordinary custody and return instructions. Maintenance could carry the finite operating extracts and forms for its receiving duty. Departure could carry only its own permitted observations and certificate, with no new institutional endorsement. Shared tools stayed. Yue appreciated the practical question because a travel bag made rights visible in a way an impressive title sometimes did not. She would be able to point to the actual thing she was authorized to deliver.

reservoir_ep22_049.speaker: narrator
reservoir_ep22_049.text: On the way back, Tian asked which offer the basket preferred. Yue said the basket had no vote and an ordinary job to continue here. Tian looked satisfied with that unexpected stability. He then asked the real question: would she write when she reached Lantern? Yue would send an ordinary private acknowledgment if the actual road and receiving desk allowed, paid from her own money. She gave no compulsory reply date to anybody else. The friendship could continue through particular messages rather than become a promise of instant knowledge across every future mile.

reservoir_ep22_050.speaker: narrator
reservoir_ep22_050.text: At the room, Yue prepared the private after-course purse. Twenty coppers had been reserved from actually completed personal income for ten ordinary days of food and bed beginning tomorrow. Thirty-eight more would pay the ordinary fifteen-day carrier package to Lantern when accepted: eight passage, thirty actual scheduled food and sleeping stops at two per travel day. Its departure would be Three Hundred Seventy and expected arrival Four Hundred Eighty-five. She caught the wrong hundreds in her own draft and corrected the arrival to Three Hundred Eighty-five before any booking. The route was fifteen ordinary days, not a leap through qi.

reservoir_ep22_051.speaker: narrator
reservoir_ep22_051.text: The correction embarrassed her enough to make her laugh. Accurate work did not prevent a tired mind from writing the wrong hundreds; it made checking before payment worthwhile. She asked Qiu to confirm the carrier's actual current date at the ordinary desk. The route left Three Hundred Seventy and reached Lantern on Three Hundred Eighty-five, with travel days Seventy through Eighty-four. Current ordinary inspection would still govern departure and any delay. The private package's accepted source would be read before payment. No course meal credit or new basin wage was needed to make the reserved thirty-eight available.

reservoir_ep22_052.speaker: narrator
reservoir_ep22_052.text: Yue did not pay the future carrier tonight. The actual booking would follow its current accepted route check and package terms. She retained the money privately, with enough completed income after the family journey and letters for the post-course living and road. The possible maintenance nine would remain a future receipt unless selected and its physical days actually performed. The observer three would not arrive before its two remote intervals were done. Departure had no new wage. Her choice could matter to future cash without requiring unearned money to appear in the present purse.

reservoir_ep22_053.speaker: narrator
reservoir_ep22_053.text: The final course room inspection found Yue's private drawings, clothes, certificate copy and permitted notes, with shared sample property accounted for at Jing's shelf. She would retain the ordinary bed under a new privately paid daily arrangement from tomorrow, not extend the teaching allocation because the key felt familiar. The receiver offered the posted ordinary rate and Yue accepted it from her own reserved source. The course's actual final night belonged to Fifty-nine. Tomorrow's bed and meals would have an actual private payment on their own date, and the new contract choice would be separate.

reservoir_ep22_054.speaker: narrator
reservoir_ep22_054.text: Before the lamp was lowered, Fu knocked with the plain boot cord's spare end. She offered it as a small ordinary mending gift from her own purchase and asked whether Yue wanted it. Yue accepted and promised no particular future use. The offered object became hers because its owner chose to give it, unlike a sample sleeve or a worker's tool that had merely been used near her. The distinction had become familiar enough to feel gentle. They laughed about the retired crooked knot and said good night without requiring a final speech.

reservoir_ep22_055.speaker: narrator
reservoir_ep22_055.text: Jing stopped at the door to confirm tomorrow's ordinary receiving hour and wished Yue a sound choice. Yue asked what that meant. Jing said a choice she could describe accurately beside its actual duties, not one whose losses vanished in a pleasant heading. The answer suited their months together. Yue thanked her and said she would read the exact dates again before signing. The certificate had made one stage true. The next role would need a new decision about work, money, data and departure, with other people's consent still intact.

reservoir_ep22_056.speaker: narrator
reservoir_ep22_056.text: Deng sent no extra lesson task for the course's last night. His paid instruction had ended, and any later unfamiliar application would need its own qualified arrangement. Yue could practice the earned familiar settling safely within its known scope, with no new range hidden in the title. She did so briefly and stopped. The body felt ordinary rather than invincible. It carried an independently tested balanced reservoir, a limited shoulder and the need for sleep. She liked knowing the actual combination could be useful without pretending the certificate described another person entirely.

reservoir_ep22_057.speaker: narrator
reservoir_ep22_057.text: Outside, the garden bird hung beside the bean supports while the public bay lamp shone at its current site. Yue's selected water role had left its own real result and unanswered concern. The family visit had left its own completed conversations and actual absences. The course had delivered care, wages and evidence. None was erased by stage eight or gathered into one spotless history. The ordinary future would ask new questions. She could meet them with a better-tested practice and the same habit of checking which actual person or source held the answer.

reservoir_ep22_058.speaker: narrator
reservoir_ep22_058.text: The final meal and bed marks were accepted before midnight on Fifty-nine, closing the finite course at its real end. The returned unused family-absence meal credits remained with the teaching source. No shared balance entered Yue's private purse at closure. The independent record stayed with its custodian; the issued copy stayed with her. Tomorrow she would pay privately for ordinary living and hear a finite new offer. A completed season of work could end cleanly without pretending every relationship or unresolved household need had also reached a perfect final sentence.

reservoir_ep22_059.speaker: narrator
reservoir_ep22_059.text: Yue placed the three prepared contracts on the low table with their actual budgets and dates visible. Rotation meant limited comparative rights and two later receiving intervals. Maintenance meant local ordinary work and later operating duties. Departure meant completed wages and own notes without endorsement. She wanted different parts of each and could accept only one. The choice would change actual opportunities after the certificate, leaving her earned practice the same. She lowered the lamp, settled the balanced reservoir within its old input ceiling and slept before the real new morning.

reservoir_ep22_060.speaker: narrator
reservoir_ep22_060.text: On One Thousand Three Hundred Sixty, the private room receiver waited for the first actual after-course payment and Qiu waited at the separate contract desk. Yue had the completed personal source for the day's two coppers. The owners had the common eighteen for one accepted water-service choice or its return. Her new stage did not merge those purses. She rose from the ordinary bed, kept the shoulder comfortable and took the prepared contracts to breakfast. Today the next role would become real work or a real declined opportunity, rather than remain a useful possibility she could imagine owning.

reservoir_ep22_061.speaker: narrator
reservoir_ep22_061.text: The bakery counter smelled of onions and warm crust. Liu Tong offered to slice Yue's breakfast bread rather than make her lift the long knife at an awkward angle. She accepted and held the plate steady below her comfortable range. Behind them, an argument over the best place for the new flower jar ended in laughter when nobody could move it without wetting a sleeve. The ordinary room made space for several wants at once. Yue would still have to decide which offered task she could honestly take with her.

reservoir_ep22_062.speaker: narrator
reservoir_ep22_062.text: She reread the receiving dates while eating slowly. The future letters would be work, with named hours and finite authority, even though they involved no heavy waterstaff. The local maintenance days would occupy actual mornings and afternoons before departure. Refusing both would leave time free and comparative access closed. She could feel the difference as strongly as the taste of the onions. Finite work had become familiar enough to be tempting; a free interval had become valuable enough to defend.

reservoir_ep22_063.speaker: narrator
reservoir_ep22_063.text: When breakfast ended, she folded the clean napkin and walked to the contract desk. The day's separate room payment and water-service decision awaited her. The owners sat beside the open window.
